I’m truly sorry to hear about the difficulties you’ve faced, particularly during such a challenging time following the loss of your Mum. Supporting patients and their families through such circumstances is something we take very seriously, and I’m sorry to hear that you felt let down.
As the Practice Manager, this is the first time I’m hearing of these concerns. Had I been made aware at the time, I would have welcomed the opportunity to discuss the issues with you directly and work toward a resolution.
We understand how distressing it can be when care doesn’t meet expectations, and I would still very much like to talk with you about your experience so we can look into what happened and see how we might be able to support you moving forward.
If you feel comfortable doing so, please don’t hesitate to contact me at the practice.

However, the GP must agree to this before shared care can begin. If a GP feels unqualified or unsupported in managing the treatment, they are not obligated to accept shared care. The prescribing clinician is ultimately responsible for the patient's safety. If shared care is declined, the specialist must continue prescribing and monitoring the medication.
We have based our decision on current guidance from the BMA and LMC, which we have provided to you personally.

We understand that this may be disappointing news, but please be assured that this decision was made with your safety and well-being in mind. Our priority is to ensure the most appropriate and safe care for all our patients.
